iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State clearance, volume of distribution, half-life, and steady state.
agents.II: Derive the one-compartment IV bolus model and the steady-state concentration.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rowland & Tozer, Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical dosing (field 335). Trap: must not claim half-life alone sets the dosing interval.

agents.I: State docking/scoring, binding pockets, and lead selectivity.
agents.II: Derive the free-energy of binding from the molecular mechanics terms.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Anderson 2003; Leach, Molecular Modelling.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline synthesis (field 261). Trap: must not claim a docking score is a binding affinity.

agents.I: State CYP450 metabolism, the ADME cascade, and reactive metabolites.
agents.II: Derive the Michaelis-Menten clearance of a CYP substrate and the inhibition constant.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Parkinson & Ogilvie, Biotransformation of Xenobiotics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical safety (field 342). Trap: must not claim in-vitro clearance predicts in-vivo without scaling.

agents.I: State dose-response, the therapeutic window, and drug interactions.
agents.II: Derive the loading-dose and maintenance-dose equations from the PK parameters.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Atkinson et al., Principles of Clinical Pharmacology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline PK modeling (field 332). Trap: must not claim a drug is safe across populations without adjustment.

agents.I: State CYP2D6/CYP2C19 phenotypes and label-based dosing.
agents.II: Derive the phenotype-to-genotype translation and the activity score.
agents.III: Situate the theory: CPIC guidelines; Evans & Relling 1999.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline population genetics (field 292). Trap: must not claim a genotype fully determines response.

agents.I: State bioavailability routes, controlled release, and nanocarrier targeting.
agents.II: Derive the zero-order release kinetics of a controlled-release matrix.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Allen & Cullis 2004 (lipid nanoparticles).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline formulation chemistry (field 245). Trap: must not claim an in-vitro release profile predicts in-vivo behavior.

agents.I: State neurotransmitter synthesis/reuptake targets and receptor occupancy.
agents.II: Derive the occupancy model of receptor binding and its therapeutic index.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Nestler, Hyman, Malenka, Molecular Neuropharmacology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline psychiatry (field 315). Trap: must not claim immediate binding predicts clinical effect.

agents.I: State resistance mechanisms and PK/PD indices (fT>MIC).
agents.II: Derive the fT>MIC index and the mutant-selection window.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rotschafer et al.; Mandell (antimicrobial chapters).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical ID (field 320). Trap: must not claim an antibiotic's spectrum is fixed.

agents.I: State chemotherapy cell-cycle specificity, TKIs, and biomarker-selected trials.
agents.II: Derive the dose-response of a targeted inhibitor from the receptor-occupancy model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: DeVita; Druker et al. 2001 (imatinib).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical oncology (field 313). Trap: must not claim targeted agents are free of systemic toxicity.

agents.I: State ML-based scoring, generative chemistry, and ADMET models.
agents.II: Derive the docking scoring function and the ML potential-energy surrogate.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Vanathevan et al. 2019.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cheminformatics (field 252). Trap: must not claim a generated molecule is synthesizable or safe.

agents.I: State causality assessment and signal detection.
agents.II: Derive the disproportionality analysis (ROR) and its confidence intervals.
agents.III: Situate the theory: WHO-UMC; Bate & Evans 2009.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline toxicology (field 334). Trap: must not claim a signal is a confirmed causal effect.

agents.I: State the radiation budget, feedbacks, and climate sensitivity.
agents.II: Derive the equilibrium climate sensitivity from the energy-balance model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hartmann, Global Physical Climatology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline weather forecasting (field 344). Trap: must not claim a single model's projection is a prediction.

agents.I: State the governing equations, fronts, and cyclones.
agents.II: Derive the quasi-geostrophic omega equation and its vertical-motion signature.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Holton & Hakim, An Introduction to Dynamic Meteorology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline climate projections (field 343). Trap: must not claim a forecast beyond its skill horizon.

agents.I: State the thermohaline circulation, the Coriolis effect, and Ekman transport.
agents.II: Derive the Ekman spiral and the total Ekman transport.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Talley et al., Descriptive Physical Oceanography.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline marine ecology (field 361). Trap: must not claim ocean heat change is linear with surface temperature.

agents.I: State carbon pools, fluxes, and residence times.
agents.II: Derive the box-model carbon budget and the oceanic uptake lag.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Schlesinger & Bernhardt, Biogeochemistry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ecosystem ecology (field 359). Trap: must not claim emission cuts instantly lower atmospheric CO2.

agents.I: State glacier mass balance, ice-sheet dynamics, and sea-level contribution.
agents.II: Derive the shallow-ice approximation and the ice-sheet thickness profile.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cuffey & Paterson, The Physics of Glaciers.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline paleoclimate (field 348). Trap: must not claim ice-sheet collapse is linear or predictable.

agents.I: State proxy records and the CO2-temperature relationship.
agents.II: Derive the delta-O18 temperature calibration from the fractionation equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bradley, Paleoclimatology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline modern climate (field 343). Trap: must not claim a proxy is a direct thermometer.

agents.I: State plate tectonics, the rock cycle, and fault slip styles.
agents.II: Derive the isostasy condition and the crustal thickness from the Airy model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Marshak, Earth: Portrait of a Planet.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline seismology (field 350). Trap: must not claim a rock's age from one isotope system without closure assumptions.

agents.I: State P/S wave propagation and moment magnitude; focal mechanisms.
agents.II: Derive the moment magnitude from the seismic moment and the Gutenberg-Richter relation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shearer, Introduction to Seismology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline structural geology (field 349). Trap: must not claim earthquakes are predictable.

agents.I: State magma dynamics, eruption styles, and hazard maps.
agents.II: Derive the conduit-flow model of magma ascent and the eruption velocity.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sigurdsson et al., The Encyclopedia of Volcanoes.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline melt geochemistry (field 349). Trap: must not claim an eruption forecast is certain.

agents.I: State the water balance and Darcy's law; define baseflow.
agents.II: Derive Darcy's law and the groundwater flow equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dingman, Physical Hydrology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline water-quality chemistry (field 368). Trap: must not claim a model's recharge estimate is exact.

agents.I: State soil horizons, texture classes, and cation exchange capacity.
agents.II: Derive the water-retention curve model and the field-capacity estimate.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Brady & Weil, The Nature and Properties of Soils.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline agronomy (field 470). Trap: must not claim fertility is fixed by texture.

agents.I: State gravity/magnetics surveys and GNSS plate motion.
agents.II: Derive the free-air gravity anomaly and the isostatic correction.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lowrie, Fundamentals of Geophysics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline seismology (field 350). Trap: must not claim a geophysical inversion is unique.

agents.I: State multispectral indices (NDVI) and SAR interferometry.
agents.II: Derive the NDVI and the InSAR phase-to-displacement relation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Campbell & Wynne, Introduction to Remote Sensing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline image models (field 100). Trap: must not claim an index value is a direct biophysical measurement.

agents.I: State return periods, event attribution, and compound events.
agents.II: Derive the return-period estimate from the generalized extreme value distribution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: IPCC AR6 WG1 ch. 11; Merz et al. 2020.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline insurance pricing (field 391). Trap: must not claim a single event is 'caused by' climate change without attribution.

agents.I: State ozone chemistry (NOx/VOC) and aerosol formation.
agents.II: Derive the steady-state ozone production in the polluted boundary layer.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Seinfeld & Pandis, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline chemistry-climate coupling (field 343). Trap: must not claim a local AQI captures all health-relevant exposures.

agents.I: State species interactions, the niche concept, and diversity indices.
agents.II: Derive the Lotka-Volterra competition equations and the coexistence condition.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Morin, Community Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline population dynamics (field 367). Trap: must not claim a species correlation implies interaction.

agents.I: State productivity, nutrient cycling, and trophic cascades.
agents.II: Derive the nutrient-retention model of an ecosystem and its equilibrium.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Chapin et al., Principles of Terrestrial Ecosystem Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline biogeochemistry (field 346). Trap: must not claim ecosystem services are fungible.

agents.I: State IUCN categories, minimum viable populations, and protected-area design.
agents.II: Derive the minimum viable population from the extinction-risk model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Primack, Essentials of Conservation Biology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline environmental law (field 435). Trap: must not claim reserve presence implies persistence.

agents.I: State pelagic/benthic zones, reef dynamics, and MPA design.
agents.II: Derive the fisheries yield model (Schaefer) and the maximum sustainable yield.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bertness et al., Marine Community Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline oceanography (field 345). Trap: must not claim an MPA instantly restores stocks.

agents.I: State lotic vs lentic systems and eutrophication drivers.
agents.II: Derive the phosphorus-loading model of lake eutrophication.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dodds & Whiles, Freshwater Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline water treatment (field 484). Trap: must not claim nutrient cuts immediately fix blooms.

agents.I: State range shifts, phenological change, and climate velocity.
agents.II: Derive the climate-velocity metric and the leading-edge migration rate.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Parmesan & Yohe 2003; Root et al. 2003.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline climate modeling (field 343). Trap: must not claim a range shift is purely climate-driven.

agents.I: State reference ecosystems, successional trajectories, and intervention thresholds.
agents.II: Derive a successional-trajectory model and its restoration endpoint.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Clewell & Aronson, Ecological Restoration.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline landscaping (field 196). Trap: must not claim a restored site equals the original.

agents.I: State adaptation, trade-offs, life histories, and evolutionarily stable strategies.
agents.II: Derive the optimal clutch size from the Lack model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Stearns, The Evolution of Life Histories.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline population genetics (field 292). Trap: must not claim optimality models predict every trait.

agents.I: State optimal foraging and signal honesty.
agents.II: Derive the marginal-value theorem for patch residence time.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Krebs & Davies, An Introduction to Behavioural Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline psychology (field 420). Trap: must not claim lab behavior occurs in the wild.

agents.I: State the logistic model, the Leslie matrix, and the Allee effect.
agents.II: Derive the logistic growth equilibrium and the Leslie-matrix growth rate.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gotelli, A Primer of Ecology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline harvest management (field 360). Trap: must not claim a carrying capacity is fixed.

agents.I: State dose-response curves, bioaccumulation, and NOEL.
agents.II: Derive the bioaccumulation factor at steady state from uptake and elimination rates.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Newman, Fundamentals of Ecotoxicology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline human toxicology (field 334). Trap: must not claim lab thresholds transfer to field mixtures.

agents.I: State the EIA process and the precautionary principle.
agents.II: Derive a cost-benefit analysis of an environmental regulation and its discounting.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Glasson et al., Introduction to Environmental Impact Assessment.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline environmental law (field 435). Trap: must not claim an EIA guarantees protection.

agents.I: State the urban heat island, fragmentation, and green infrastructure.
agents.II: Derive the urban heat-island intensity from the energy-balance model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Pickett et al. 2011.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline urban economics (field 384). Trap: must not claim green roofs fully offset urban emissions.
